content.title: About
content.content: Pompano is a marine fish from the family Carangidae, found in warm coastal waters of the Atlantic and Pacific oceans. When baked or broiled with a coating, it offers tender white flesh, a mildly sweet flavor, and a crisp crust.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pompano is often called the “golden fish” because of its golden‑hued skin.
It is a staple in Caribbean and Southeast Asian cuisines.
In the wild, pompano can reach up to 70 cm in length and weigh about 4 kg.
The flesh is rich in omega‑3 fatty acids, beneficial for heart health.
Proper coating techniques keep the crust crunchy even after baking.

items.title: Rich in omega‑3
items.content: Omega‑3 fatty acids help lower triglyceride levels and support cardiovascular health.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: A 100‑g serving provides about 20 g of complete protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Pompano supplies vitamin B12, niacin, and riboflavin, which are important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: It contains selenium, phosphorus, and potassium, supporting immune function and bone health.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Compared with red meat, pompano has low saturated fat, making it suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to seafood, including pompano.

items.title: Heavy‑metal contamination
items.content: Like many marine fish, pompano can accumulate mercury; moderate consumption is advised, especially for children and pregnant women.

items.title: Overconsumption
items.content: Large portions may lead to excess calories and fat intake despite the fish’s healthy profile.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Bake the fish at 180 °C for 12‑15 minutes after coating it in breadcrumbs, spices, and a drizzle of olive oil. For pan‑searing, cook 3‑4 minutes per side until golden. Serve with lemon wedges, fresh herbs, and a light vegetable side.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep fresh pompano refrigerated at 0‑2 °C, wrapped in plastic film, and use within 2 days. Frozen fish can be stored up to 3 months at –18 °C. Before cooking, check for a fresh sea scent; a strong ammonia odor indicates spoilage.
